Conducting Gel

During aesthetic and medical procedures, many experts use a transparent and liquid sticky product for the skin; this product makes it easier for the skin tightening machine to slide and spread the gel. This product is called conductive serum for microcurrent; it enhances the electron conductivity of the medical aesthetic device when they contact the skin. Conductive serums are also used during medical processes such as electrocardiograms and ultrasound but are also used for aesthetic treatments using ultrasound processes such as radiofrequency or pulsed light.

Uses Of Conductive Gel For Microcurrent

Sound waves produced by the ultrasound or skin tightening machine require a conductor to work efficiently. This gel reduces the electrical resistance between the electrodes and skin, enhancing the signal transmission, resulting in higher accuracy of the results acquired. It is necessary for processes such as ultrasound scans, without it, it would be impossible to get good images. It also prevents irritations that normally occur due to the rubbing of the electrodes.

Many gels also have moisturizing properties that keep the skin hydrated during the aesthetic process. And although some experts stated that it enhances the absorption of the ingredients by the skin, there is not enough research to back this claim.

Properties Of Conductive Gel

The best conductive gel for microcurrent consists of a gelatinous or liquid texture and appearance. It also has neutral pH and does not smell since it is viscous and does not slide on the skin.

During the medical process, the cosmetic expert will apply it to the skin before initiating the cosmetic treatment process. And although it is sticky, it can be removed easily from the skin because it is not greasy.

When the conductive gel is used for aesthetic radiofrequency treatments, the energy is distributed, and the skin resistance is also reduced, making it the best barrier for sound waves.

Many health experts also use it for laser treatments for hair removal, such as intense pulsed light. In this case, the gel will enhance the light transmission through the skin and decrease the heat going to the skin's surface.

When Is The Best Time To Use Conductive Gel?

As mentioned, this conductive gel is required for medical aesthetic processes. When focusing on aesthetic medication, it is used with radiofrequency, although it is essential to differentiate between monopolar and bipolar as well as in monopolar between resistive and capacitive.

In the bipolar radiofrequency, as the 2 electrodes are close, using the conductive gel will be ideal for transmitting the electricity; with this, a short circuit will be produced between the electrodes. Hence the energy will flow through the gel rather than through the skin. So, when glycerin is used, since it is less conductive and is a brake on the gel, the health experts will put more pressure on the skin instead of gently rubbing it on the skin’s surface.

In resistive monopolar radiofrequency, cosmetic experts look for the best conduction. Hence not having another electrode nearby allows them to use the conducting gel more effectively.

For the capacitive monopolar, the electrodes are insulated. Hence there will not be any direct electrical conduction. It is performed through capacitance; it is a type of jumping energy that occurs through the insulator; it will then interact with the initial layer of the skin. In this, the cream is generally used, which makes it easier for the skin tightening machine to seamlessly slide on the head.

During laser treatments, like hair removal, a gel that is a surface gel alternative is used to make sure that the machine can easily slide without any risk of crystal remaining separated from the skin since it can burn if it occurs.
